subject: characteristics of latent field in INLA

messages.author: 929e733ff7821ad3
messages.subject: characteristics of latent field in INLA
parts:
Dear all,

I have a questions regarding the characteristics of latent field. 

According to the green book (Spatial and Spatio-temporal Bayesian Models with R-INLA, by Blangiardo.et.al), page 108.

if \boldsymbol{\mathbf{\theta}} represent the latent field, for the likelihood function: "each data point y_i is connected to only one element theta_i in the latent field". I didnt get this statement clearly. In an example of linear regression with 200 observations, with latent field (beta_0 and beta_1). Does this statement mean that the likelihood of observation 1  (y_1) is dependent on (beta_0) and  likelihood of observation 2  (y_2) is dependent on (beta_1)? This does not make sense. If the latent field is \boldsymbol{\theta}=\{\beta_0, \boldsymbol{\mathbf{\beta},f}\}, does theta_i refer to \theta_0 or the set of \boldsymbol{\theta} corresponding to observation i.

If we write \boldsymbol{\theta} into a discrete matrix, it is a n*K matrix with n the number of observations and K the total number of latent parameters? what's the dimensionality of the precision matrix for  \boldsymbol{\theta}?

Thanks

Lisa

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] characteristics of latent field in INLA
parts:
Hi,

what is done, it also to introduce the linear predictor itself into the
latent field.

if

y ~ 1 + x

then we have the intercept b0 and the regression coof for x, b1.
additionally we introduce

eta = b0*1 + b1*x

so the latent field is

(eta, b0, b1)


to avoid singularity, we add a little noise so that

eta|... ~ N(b0*1 + b1*x, tiny.noise)

then y[i] only depend on eta[i].

this is also discussed in the original inla-paper, 2009.

Best
H

messages.author: 929e733ff7821ad3
messages.subject: Re: characteristics of latent field in INLA
parts:
Thanks Rue for the quick answer, I will consult your paper.

I have another question regarding the GMRF property of latent field. Maybe it's better to address it in an example: suppose u_s and u_s+1 are two locations in the spatial distribution and these two are two of the latent variables. The final output of INLA gives the posterior marginal distributions of p(u_s|Y) and p(u_s+1|Y). Are these two distributions supposed to be independent, according to conditionally independent property? thus, p(u_s, u_s+1|Y)=p(u_s|Y)*p(u_s+1|Y). If not, based on what properties are they not independent?

thanks very much

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: characteristics of latent field in INLA
parts:
They are not independent because of
- hyperparameters
- prior covariance structure (spatial model)
- conditioning on data (e.g. the data may inform you that one should be larger than the other)

Kind regards,
Haakon
